title: Benchmark ops standup — raw notes and next actions
body:
ATTENDEES: Liam Chen (owner), Anita Sharma (profiling), Miguel Torres (batching), Priya Nair (rollouts), Ethan Park (observability)

GOAL: quick sync on recent throughput/latency regressions observed on s-4g-prod (night window 2025-07-14 -> spike at 02:10 UTC). Capture raw observations, reproduce plan, and allocate action owners.

SUMMARY:
- Regression: p99 latency for text-generation (gpt-variants, seq=1024) increased from 420ms -> 510ms (≈21% increase) during a narrow window overnight. Baseline p50 stable. Throughput (tokens/s) dropped by ~12% on the same jobs.
- Suspected correlates: new libcudnn kernel selector change merged in GH PR #492 (commit abc123f), a config default change to continuous-batching timeout from 8ms -> 12ms, and a transient NVMe spike on node infra-7.
- Repro status: can reproduce locally on a dedicated dev rig with the newer build and a synthetic load that mirrors prefix-heavy traffic. Cannot reproduce on canary (s-4g-canary) which uses quantized model variant vq2.

RAW METRICS (snippet from bench-agent logs, timestamped)
[2025-07-15 02:09:58.321] worker-12 REQUEST id=9f2a token_seq=1024 model=gpt-7b variant=fp16 kernel=autoselect p50=390 p95=470 p99=510 qps=58
[2025-07-15 02:10:02.114] runtime TRACE: KV_CACHE_HIT=0.32 BATCH_SIZE=3 avg_lat=480ms batch_wait=12.4ms
[2025-07-15 02:10:03.009] infra NVME_IOPS spike node=infra-7 iops=71500 -> baseline 12k

EXPERIMENTS RUN DURING STANDUP: (commands & quick outcomes)
- Disable new kernel selector and force old kernel: run bench-runner --model gpt-7b --seq 1024 --kernel=legacy --runs 100 -> p99 returned to 422ms. (owner: Anita)
- Revert continuous-batching timeout to 8ms: bench-runner --config batch_timeout_ms=8 -> p99 430ms. (owner: Miguel)
- Run with quantized variant vq2 on same node: bench-runner --variant vq2 -> p99 395ms, throughput +15%. (owner: Priya)
- Synthetic NVMe load reproduction: fio --name=stress --iodepth=32 --randread -> caused local node to show increased latencies but not identical pattern to prod. (owner: Ethan)

INTERPRETATION / HYPOTHESES:
1) Primary: kernel selector change picks a different convolution kernel path which increases kernel latency for long sequences in some GPU driver combinations (observed on nodes with driver 545.20).
2) Secondary: increased batch_wait due to batch_timeout bump amplifies p99 when combined with kernel change.
3) Tertiary: Storage IO noise on infra-7 amplified GC/epoch alignment leading to rare stalls (lower confidence).

IMMEDIATE ACTIONS (owners + due dates):
- Rollback kernel selector change on prod (hotfix): patch & deploy to s-4g-prod in next maintenance window (owner: Anita, due: 2025-07-16).
- Revert batch_timeout default to 8ms in config service (owner: Miguel, due: 2025-07-16).
- Add targeted bench-suite: long-seq (512/1024/2048) across driver matrix and quantization states; include p50/p95/p99 and batch_wait percentiles (owner: Priya, due: 2025-07-20).
- Observe infra-7 NVMe telemetry and correlate with perf traces; add specific alert to SRE if iops>50k for >2min (owner: Ethan, due: 2025-07-17).
- Open regression PR to add an e2e check in CI that runs 200 short-sample runs for seq=1024 on each merge to main (owner: Liam, linked: GH PR #492).

NOTES ON REPRO STEPS (devs):
1) Checkout commit abc123f and the previous commit def456a to toggle kernel selector.
2) Use bench-runner with --trace-kvcache and --emit-batch-wait to capture fine-grained timings.
3) For driver matrix testing use docker images: redwood/gpu:driver-545.20 and redwood/gpu:driver-530.85.
4) Collect perf counters via nsys sample command: nsys profile --stats true --output nvprof-run --target-processes all --capture-range cublas -- bench-runner ...

DECISIONS MADE IN-MEETING:
- Hotfix rollback of kernel selector approved (low-risk rollback).
- Do NOT change quantization defaults; encourage customers to test vq2 but keep default unchanged until more matrix data.
- Add two new regression labels in jira: perf-regression and driver-sensitive. Ticket created: SRV-1248 (owner: Liam).

OPEN QUESTIONS / RISK ITEMS:
- Why canary did not show regression if kernel selector was merged cluster-wide? (Possibility: canary uses different driver or uses prefix-aware caching).
- If driver 545.20 becomes default across fleet we need an extra QA gate for kernel selector changes.
- Long-term: consider GPU microbenchmark harness to test kernel selector combos pre-merge.

FOLLOWUPS (weekly cadence):
- Next deep-dive: 2025-07-17 09:30 PT. Agenda: results from driver matrix, infra-7 telemetry, and CI e2e patch.
- Deliverable by 2025-07-20: matrix spreadsheet + recommendation doc for kernel selector policy (keep/opt-out per driver).

APPENDIX (quick links & snippets):
- Quick repro command: git checkout abc123f && bazel build //bench:bench-runner && ./bazel-bin/bench/bench-runner --model=gpt-7b --seq=1024 --runs=500 --emit-batch-wait --trace-kvcache
- Observability trace url (prod): https://observability.redwood/team/serving-runtime/traces?traceId=9f2a (permissioned)
- Related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/492

NOTES TO SELF: keep raw log excerpts in /tmp/bench-logs/jul15 for curious follow-up; rename artifact before uploading to GH due to size limits.

END OF NOTES
